scope: Proposition 4.6 (Prepared reverse links) of the manuscript “Finite congruence lattices: characterization and undecidability” (preprints/Finite-Congruence-Lattices-Characterization-and-Undecidability-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 206 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d26d6cd6285de4f2), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 14-15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: If X is a nonempty flat of rank at most m in a trunk chart, the reverse ideal with top X, denoted [0, X], is graded, atomistic, and coatomistic. Its strict interior has at least two horizontal comparability components, each containing comparable distinct elements. The following additional properties hold for L and for every such prepared link. (i) Every bottom interval of length two is a diamond Mb with b ≥ 3 atoms, where b − 1 ≥ 2 is not a prime power. (ii) In every interior component there is an element y two ranks below the interval’s top whose upper interval is a diamond with at least two middle elements. 14 In addition, L has the following separation property: (iii) For any atom u and any proper upper bound ω ≥ u, there is a rank-two element z ≥ u with z ̸≤ ω.
